sections.title: Humanizing Data: Storytelling, Folklore and Ethnography
sections.description: How can stories illuminate human experiences? How can patterns in data amplify the power of storytelling? This course examines narrative, folklore and ethnographic research, as well as their intersection, providing students with the tools to uncover, analyze, and communicate complex aspects of human experience. By combining storytelling techniques and ethnographic inquiry, students will learn to transform data-driven insights into compelling narratives that resonate with multiple audiences.

sections.title: Humanizing Data: Storytelling and Quantitative Ethnography
sections.description: How can stories help us better understand human experience? How can patterns in data deepen our understanding of education? This course engages students in a semester-long writing process that explores the personal and human connections they develop through the study of education. Students will learn to interpret lived experiences through narrative inquiry and examine patterns in qualitative data from a quantitative ethnographic perspective. Throughout the semester, students will analyze, write, and present their work as they develop an autoethnography. By bringing together ethnographic inquiry and quantitative approaches to qualitative data, students will learn to communicate the complexity of human experience in ways that are both analytically rigorous and deeply human.
